name: LeadCop Disposable Email Checker
author: Leadcop

sections.description:
LeadCop Disposable Email Checker blocks disposable email addresses, role accounts and fake signups on WooCommerce checkout, WordPress registration and contact forms. It connects your site to the LeadCop API for real-time email verification, so temporary burner emails never reach your database, your mailing list or your CRM.

Who it’s for

  • WooCommerce store owners who want to stop fake orders, coupon abuse and repeat free-trial signups made with throwaway addresses.
  • Membership, SaaS and course sites that need real email addresses at user registration.
  • Marketers and agencies who collect leads through contact forms and newsletter forms and want clean lists, better email deliverability and a protected sender reputation.
  • B2B businesses that only want work email addresses, not free providers like Gmail or Yahoo.

What you use it for

  • Spam protection on registration, comment, checkout and contact forms.
  • Email verification at the moment someone types or submits their address.
  • Keeping disposable email addresses out of WooCommerce orders and marketing lists.

Third Party Services

LeadCop Disposable Email Checker relies on the LeadCop.io service to validate email addresses. During validation requests, the plugin transmits metadata and email addresses to the LeadCop API servers.

The plugin sends the following data to LeadCop.io when email validation is performed:

  • Email address submitted by the user
  • Website URL (used to verify API authorization and domain ownership)
  • Validation metadata (form integration type and request source)

This data is transmitted securely over HTTPS and is used solely for email validation, disposable email detection, role-account detection, free email provider detection, and domain/TLD validation.

For details on data handling and user privacy, please refer to the:
* Privacy Policy: https://leadcop.io/privacy-policy
* Terms of Service: https://leadcop.io/terms-of-service

Key Features

  • Disposable Email Detection – Automatically rejects temporary, single-use, and burner email addresses (e.g. Mailinator, TempMail).
  • Role Email Detection – Detects and blocks generic team alias mailboxes (e.g., info@, sales@, support@) or warns users depending on your policy.
  • Free Provider Detection – Optionally filters consumer accounts (gmail.com, yahoo.com) to force business/work signups on B2B forms.
  • Invalid TLD Detection – Blocks invalid domain extensions/TLDs to prevent typing errors and invalid domains.
  • Spam Protection – Blocks bots, spammers, and fake domains from registering accounts or submitting forms.
  • Allowlist – Domains and addresses on your LeadCop Allowlist (paid plans, managed in your LeadCop dashboard) always pass, even if another rule would block them.
  • WooCommerce Checkout & Registration Protection – Native integration to prevent checkout blockages or fake sales orders from temporary emails.
  • Newsletter Protection – Includes a simple shortcode [leadcop_subscribe] and widget to capture and validate newsletter subscribers.
  • Onboarding Assistant – Quick setup wizard guides you from API key entry to active form protection in less than 2 minutes.

Supported Forms

LeadCop works with these forms and plugins out of the box:

  • WordPress User Registration
  • WordPress Comments
  • WooCommerce Checkout & Registration
  • Contact Form 7
  • WPForms (Lite & Pro)
  • Gravity Forms
  • Elementor Pro Forms
  • Ninja Forms
  • Fluent Forms
  • Formidable Forms
  • Forminator
  • WS Form (Lite & Pro)
  • LeadCop Newsletter form ([leadcop_subscribe] shortcode)

Each integration can be turned on or off from the LeadCop settings page.

Using a form that isn’t listed, or one that isn’t working? Email us at Support@leadcop.io with the form plugin name and we’ll look into it.

Developer-Friendly

Includes the leadcop_validate_email() helper function for custom themes and custom forms. Done completely server-side, ensuring your API key is not exposed in public scripts.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the leadcop-disposable-email-checker folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install through Plugins → Add New by uploading the zip file.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to the LeadCop menu in your WordPress admin dashboard and follow the onboarding wizard.
  4. Input your API key, click Save Settings to automatically validate connection, and toggle your desired integrations.
sections.faq:
Do I need a LeadCop account?

Yes. Sign up at leadcop.io to obtain your API key. A free tier is available to get you started.

Does the plugin support country blocking?

No. LeadCop country rules work with the LeadCop website script only. The plugin checks emails from your WordPress server, so LeadCop sees your server’s location rather than the visitor’s. To block by country, add the LeadCop script to your site (you can keep this plugin installed) and set your countries in the LeadCop dashboard under Script settings → Country Rules.

Is this plugin GDPR compliant?

The plugin includes privacy disclosures and integrates with WordPress privacy policy tools. Site owners are responsible for ensuring compliance with applicable privacy regulations and should disclose that email addresses may be transmitted to LeadCop.io for validation.

Will this slow down my forms or checkout?

Each validation call adds a small, optimized network request (typically under 200ms). If you enable the live client-side validation, verification happens in the background when a user clicks out of the email field, preventing checkout delay.

What happens if the LeadCop API is unreachable?

The plugin fails open. If your site cannot reach the LeadCop API due to a network timeout, the form submission is allowed through. Your site’s core functionality is not interrupted.

Which form builders are supported?

WordPress User Registration, WordPress Comments, WooCommerce (Checkout & Registration), Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms, Elementor Pro Forms, Ninja Forms, Fluent Forms, Formidable Forms, Forminator and WS Form. See Supported Forms above for the full list.

My form isn’t listed or isn’t blocking emails. What should I do?

Email Support@leadcop.io and tell us which form plugin you’re using and the page where the form is. We’ll help you get it working, and we regularly add new form integrations based on requests.

Is there a limit on how many emails are checked?

Every email is checked when a form is submitted, with no limit from the plugin. Your only limit is your LeadCop plan’s monthly checks.

The live check (the instant ✓/✗ badge shown while someone types) has a small limit for visitors who are not logged in to your WordPress site: 10 checks per visitor every 10 minutes, and 300 per hour for the whole site. This stops bots from using up your credits. When the limit is reached, the badge is not shown, but the email is still checked on submit. Logged-in users have no limit.

To raise the hourly limit, add this to your theme’s functions.php:
add_filter( ‘leadcop_live_check_hourly_cap’, fn() => 2000 );

Is my API key secure?

The API key is stored in the WordPress options table, and all API calls are executed server-side via PHP. It is not exposed in client-side scripts.
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • New: local Allowlist in Settings → Real-Time Protection Filters. Addresses and domains listed there always pass every rule, are checked on your site before calling LeadCop (so they use no credits), and take effect immediately with no cache delay.
  • New: domains and email addresses on your LeadCop Allowlist (Dashboard → Allowlist) always pass, including the plugin’s own role-address check. Results are cached for up to 24 hours, so a newly allowlisted address may take that long to pass on forms where it was already checked.
  • Security: limits on the live email check, so bots can’t use up your LeadCop credits. The live check is the instant ✓/✗ badge shown while someone types their email. The limits apply only to visitors who are not logged in to your WordPress site: 10 checks per visitor every 10 minutes, and 300 per hour for the whole site. Logged-in users have no limit. When a limit is reached, the badge is simply not shown. Emails are still fully checked when the form is submitted, so protection is not reduced. Developers can change the hourly limit with the leadcop_live_check_hourly_cap filter.
  • Anonymous live checks no longer store a per-address cache entry in the database; disposable-domain verdicts are cached per domain instead.
  • New: the plugin Dashboard and the “LeadCop Overview” WordPress dashboard widget now list which forms are protected right now, which are installed but turned off, and which other form plugins are supported.

1.0.4

  • Added a Supported Forms list to the plugin description, with a support contact (Support@leadcop.io) for forms that aren’t listed or aren’t working.
  • The Message Appearance error colors now also style the error shown under the email field in form builders (Contact Form 7, WPForms, Forminator, Gravity Forms, Fluent Forms, Ninja Forms, Formidable Forms, WS Form) when LeadCop blocks an address.

1.0.3

  • Added native WS Form integration: disposable and blocked emails are rejected server-side before the submission is saved, with the error shown inline on the email field.
  • Added Forminator to the list of supported form builders.

1.0.2

  • Free accounts now show “Never — one-time credits” instead of an incorrect reset date, matching the LeadCop free tier’s one-time credit allowance.
  • Renamed the billing panel’s “Renewal Reset Date” to “Credit Reset Date”.

1.0.1

  • Added a user-managed Blocked TLDs list: reject specific domain extensions (e.g. xyz, top, ru) even when the TLD is otherwise valid, with block/warn mode and a custom message.
  • Blocked-TLD rule enforces locally as a fallback when the API is unavailable.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Added onboarding steps checklist.
  • Added live account connection status card.
  • Added native integrations for WPForms, Gravity Forms, Elementor Pro Forms, and Ninja Forms.
  • Redesigned administration dashboard using LeadCop Orange brand theme.
  • Implemented automatic background connection validation on settings save.
  • Added Third-Party Service disclosures, Privacy Policy/TOS links, and GDPR compliance warnings.
  • Email validation on WP registration, comments, WooCommerce, and Contact Form 7.
  • Newsletter subscribe shortcode [leadcop_subscribe] and widget.
